title: Co-Evolving Behavioral Agents and Detectors for Adaptive Information Operations
abstract: arXiv:2611.27156v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Detectors of state-sponsored information operations (IOs) are trained on campaigns that platforms have already taken down. They lose much of their accuracy on an actor they have not seen, even though no operator in the archived data is trying to avoid them. A real operator wants two things, to reach an audience and to avoid being caught. We present IO-AI, a framework that gives simulated agents these two capabilities, engagement and evasion, and tests what each one does to detection. The agents are built from the posting behavior of real campaigns and choose the emotion, type, and timing of each post. An agent and a detector then train against each other in turn. We rank the trained agents by how hard they are to detect and train one detector on them from easiest to hardest. translated_title: 面向自适应信息行动的行为智能体与检测器协同演化方法
translated_abstract: 国家支持的信息行动（IO）检测器通常在平台已经采取下架措施的行动数据上进行训练。即使存档数据中没有任何操作者试图规避检测，这些检测器在面对未见过的行为者时也会损失大量准确性。真实的信息操作者有两个目标：触达受众和避免被发现。我们提出了IO-AI，一个赋予模拟智能体这两种能力——互动参与和规避检测——的框架，并测试每种能力对检测效果的影响。这些智能体基于真实行动的发帖行为构建，可以为每条帖子选择情绪、类型和发布时机。随后，智能体与检测器轮流进行相互对抗训练。我们按照检测难度对训练后的智能体进行排序，并按从易到难的顺序训练检测器。在20个Twitter信息行动上，该检测器相比仅在存档行动数据上训练的检测器，将对自适应智能体的漏检率降低了65%……
tldr: 该论文提出IO-AI协同演化框架，通过让基于真实信息行动行为构建、具备互动与规避能力的模拟智能体与检测器轮流对抗训练，使检测器对自适应规避智能体的漏检率降低了65%。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes IO-AI, a co-evolutionary framework in which simulated agents built from real information operation behaviors and equipped with both engagement and evasion capabilities adversarially train with detectors in turns, reducing missed detections of adaptive agents by 65% compared to detectors trained only on archived campaigns.
